question: Given ambiguous native command execution, does the observed qpos/qvel sequence after the fault distinguish delivered vs held in paired real PhysX, without accessing goal-memory fields?
evidence_not_the_method: One-step counterfactual physical indistinguishability/observable separation assay, not autonomous recovery or a learned observer
contrast: At third step issue fully converted bounded source PPO arm action to world A; issue native zero arm translation/rotation to world B; deliver identical gripper command. This is simulated actuator command divergence, not network ACK failure.
followup_diagnostic: After fault, apply identical neutral native arm and gripper actions for four further steps in both worlds; take publicly observable joint qpos and qvel at fault and after each diagnostic step.
measurement_visibility: Exclude entire 7D target_pose memory field from flat state; qpos/qvel are permitted. Native true target memory may be audited after outcomes but never enters observability measurements.
primary_stats: max_abs_qpos_gap_rad for each of 0..4 postfault steps
max_abs_qvel_gap_rad_s for each of 0..4 postfault steps
whether original source action was nonzero and bounded
native target-position and rotation divergence audit only
all original seeds, including differences equal to zero
cannot_claim: Independent-state identifiability under noisy, uncalibrated hardware sensors
sensor-model observability from a single real trajectory without an accurate counterfactual simulator
automatic recovery, motion safety, or task success gains
a new theorem or general hidden-state identifiability result
future_gate: Only if motion differences routinely exceed predeclared descriptive thresholds, implement a separately preregistered model-based classifier under controlled model mismatch and report no-readback task recovery vs optimistic/pessimistic baselines.
